newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Broad rally hands Taiwan stocks big rise at close.
newsitem.headline: Broad rally hands Taiwan stocks big rise at close.

text.p: Taiwan share prices slice through resistance to finish sharply higher on Monday, as electronics emerged to take up a charge initiated at the open by the rejuvenated financial sector, brokers said.
The index surged as high as 8,658.52 on the unexpected rally and ended at 8,640.45, a gain of 138.27 points or 1.63 percent.
Turnover was a heavy T$170 billion, a two-month high.

In an unusual twist, financials and major industrials -- and especially the bellwether electronics -- were up at the same time, prompting analysts to venture that an April-May correction was easing and that bulls of early 1997 may be running anew.
"You can see the bull run has yet to end because the market is so bullish that you can see a rare, simultaneous rise by financials and indusstrials," said Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee.
A financials rise generally is accompanied by a decline in industrial sectors and vice versa, brokers noted.

Financials opened with a bang after lagging a recent market rally, but saw their gains erode and were up only 0.53 percent at the close -- although that was still enough to provide a strong boost to the index due to the sector's heavy weighting.
China Development rose T$2 to T$123.

Electronics pushed the index through resistance at 8,600 by surging 4.17 percent. Leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor jumped the daily seven percent limit to T$102 and rival maker United Microelectronics rose T$3 to T$88.
Chipmaker Macronix International was limit-up to T$65.5 after saying on Monday it had received several foreign orders worth hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars.
Some of the orders came from key players in Europe, Japan and the United States -- including Hewlett-Packard and Philips -- Macronix administrative director Lin Yun-lung told Reuters by telephone.
